actionResult.summary: 按 159→172 审查链复核 171 新 Proposal generation：Owner Contract Reset 与重新 propose 边界合法，171 对 original strict E2 anchor 和 B1 test mutation scope 的补充方向正确，OpenSpec strict 与 package hygiene 通过；但 writer activation 仍未冻结为与 FormalFactReader 相同的 strict-admitted E2 authority，full-trailer-but-temporally-unauthorized E2 candidate 仍可成为 activation input，因此 F1-RA-001 尚未在 Proposal 层完整收敛。

reviewFindings.title: writer activation is still weaker than the original strict-admitted E2 cutover
reviewFindings.problem: 171 correctly freezes the legacy window around the original strict-admitted E2 checkpoint, but it only requires B1 writer activation to stop accepting subject-only E2 commits. Under the frozen F1 architecture, Git-only formalIdentityValid checks trailer shape while checkpoint-time Owner temporal admission is completed only by FormalFactReader. Therefore an E2 commit with a syntactically valid subject/trailer set and an owner:<64hex> value that has no matching authorize-checkpoint fact at that boundary can still be exposed by readGitBoundarySummaries and consumed by isPostE2ThreeFileWriterActive. The Proposal does not yet freeze how that consumer is bound to the same strict-admitted cutover.
reviewFindings.contractRef: 20260815-169-review-apply F1-RA-001 requiredOutcome/invariant + openspec/changes/archive-and-checkpoint-boundary/design.md Decisions 1-3 + Owner Contract Reset required outcome
reviewFindings.invariant: The migration cutover is one authority boundary: the original E2 checkpoint used for bounded legacy compatibility and for post-E2 writer activation must represent the same strict-admitted checkpoint fact. A merely trailer-shaped E2 candidate without checkpoint-time Owner authorization must not activate the writer.
evidence: design.md Decision 1 keeps git-boundary-reader.ts Git-only and explicitly assigns Owner cross-authority admission to FormalFactReader; Decision 2 defines strict admission as matching authorize-checkpoint provenance that existed at the checkpoint boundary.

design.md Decision 3 now defines the legacy anchor from strict-admitted E2 candidates, but its writer clause only says subject-only E2 checkpoints must not activate the writer; it does not reject formalIdentityValid-but-temporally-unauthorized E2 candidates.

src/services/b1-run-execution-service.ts:647-679 consumes readGitBoundarySummaries() for E2 writer activation. src/facts/git-boundary-reader.ts:142-157 can expose formalIdentityValid candidates without checking the point-in-time Owner Manifest.

Disposable fixture with Delivery Start plus an E2 checkpoint containing the complete Flowkit-Delivery/Flowkit-Change/Flowkit-Boundary trailers and a syntactically valid but nonexistent Owner-Authorization ref was returned by readGitBoundarySummaries as change-checkpoint. Removing only the subject-only E2 special case does not change this counterexample.

171 mutation scope adds the B1 test fixture but does not explicitly freeze or prove the production consumer path needed to make writer activation use the same strict-admitted anchor; an implementation that only removes the subject-only special case would still violate the 169 required outcome.
reviewFindings.impact: F1 would retain two different meanings of the E2 cutover: FormalFactReader/legacy admission would require checkpoint-time Owner authority, while B1 writer activation could switch on a Git-only candidate that is not a formal checkpoint fact. That leaves F1-RA-001 only partially closed and permits future malformed history to change writer behavior without the Owner-authorized checkpoint boundary.
reviewFindings.requiredOutcome: Revise the Proposal/Design so post-E2 writer activation is explicitly bound to the same original strict-admitted E2 cutover used by legacy compatibility, not merely to subject/trailer shape. Freeze a feasible implementation/mutation surface that preserves the Git-reader/Owner-authority separation or otherwise proves an equivalent one-authority design, and add the missing negative regression for a full-trailer E2 candidate whose Owner authorization did not exist at the boundary.
acceptance: The Proposal states one shared cutover invariant for legacy admission and writer activation: only the original strict-admitted E2 checkpoint activates the migration writer state.
A migration-lineage E2 commit with exact subject and formal trailers but no matching checkpoint-time authorize-checkpoint Owner fact does not activate the post-E2 writer.
The existing subject-only activation counterexample remains rejected, later duplicate E2 checkpoints cannot move the legacy cutover, and the real e182 strict E2 checkpoint still activates the writer.
Fresh/downstream repositories without the Flowkit internal migration lineage continue to use the current three-file writer by default.

flowkitMutationScope includes every production/test consumer actually required by the chosen design; no Git reader is turned into a second Owner-fact authority merely to avoid widening the proper consumer scope.
